newsitem.title: JAPAN: Major oil spill accidents in Japan. [CORRECTED 11:27 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Major oil spill accidents in Japan. [CORRECTED 11:27 GMT]

text.p: The following are the largest oil spill accidents in Japan since the Maritime Safety Agency started keeping records in 1971:

-- November 30, 1971. In the worst spillage accident on record in Japan, a tanker runs aground at Niigata Port on the Sea of Japan coast. (Corrects from "on the Pacific coast south of Tokyo".) Some 7,200 tonnes (50,400 barrels) of fuel oil flows out from the wreckage.

-- December 18, 1974. An oil tank explosion at Mitsubishi Oil Refinery at Mizushima Port in Okayama Prefecture on the Sea of Japan sends 7,500 to 9,500 tonnes (52,500 to 66,500 barrels) of fuel oil pouring into the sea.
-- April 6, 1977. A tanker bursts into flame after a collision off the coast of the city of Matsuyama in Ehime Prefecture on the island of Shikoku, spilling 1,200 tonnes (8,400 barrels) of crude oil.
-- October 20, 1977. A leakage in a tanker travelling off Cape Murotozaki in Kochi Prefecture in Shikoku causes a spillage of 1,300 tonnes of fuel oil (9,100 barrels).
-- October 7, 1986. A tanker collision, again off Cape Murotozaki, causes a spill of 1,380 tonnes of kerosene (9,660 barrels).
